title: Ferried-Lane IA: modular workspace switching and compact dashboard routing
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Problem: The current console navigation mixes workspace controls, long-form dashboards and rollouts in the same vertical surface which increases cognitive load and encourages deep drill paths for common tasks (view cost by model, open rollout, switch workspace). Goal: Rework information architecture to expose the three most frequent user intents — Switch context, Observe health/cost, and Control rollouts — with a lightweight, predictable interaction model.
background: Research synthesis from customer interviews (10 sessions), support ticket triage, and telemetry shows: (1) 60% of workspace switches happen within 1–2 clicks of a dashboard view, (2) console users often open rollouts from deep model pages which leads to accidental config changes, and (3) cost breakdowns are frequently accessed but not easily surfaced for fast comparisons. Existing designs in the repository focus on dense side rails and multiple nested drawers which do not scale to multi-tenant flows.
goals:
- Surface workspace switching as a first-class, low-friction control via a transient "ferry" overlay.
- Create a compact, persistent cost summary lane that sits above fold for every workspace.
- Introduce a thin, detachable ‘control lane’ for rollout actions that can be pinned or auto-collapsed.
- Preserve keyboard-first navigation and instrument telemetry for each intent flow.
non_goals:
- This ticket does not change permissioning/RBAC model.
- No backend changes to rollout API or billing aggregates are included here (engineers will be engaged for required endpoints).
proposed_flow_summary: 1) User invokes workspace ferry (keyboard shortcut or click on compact avatar) -> ferry slides from top with 3 contextual destinations; 2) Selecting a workspace temporarily overlays the compact dashboard lane which shows cost, latency, and error-rate cards; 3) Control lane exposes top-level rollout actions (canary toggle, rollback, notes) that open a focused modal for detailed edits. The ferry is ephemeral and keeps the user in the current workflow unless they choose to 'sail' to the full workspace.
success_metrics: Reduce average clicks to switch workspace from 3.2 to <=1.5
Increase visible cost-summary opens per session by 40%
Reduce accidental rollout edits by 50% in first 90 days
accessibility_considerations:
- Ferry overlay must support screen reader roles and focus trapping.
- All compact lane cards have 4.5:1 contrast for text and clear focus rings.
- Keyboard shortcut to open ferry documented and discoverable via command palette.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Chosen a top-ferry pattern (vs left persistent microrail) to minimize vertical fragmentation and support mobile narrow viewports.
- Compact cost lane uses aggregated metrics (cost, avg latency, 95p latency) to avoid overwhelming users with token-level data; detailed breakdowns remain in the cost page.
- Rollout control lane keeps destructive actions behind a focused modal to reduce accidental changes; this increases one extra click for advanced users but significantly lowers risk.
open_questions: Do we allow workspace ferry to remember last destination per user?
Should the compact cost lane be enabled by default for orgs on Dedicated?
What telemetry event naming convention for 'ferry.open' vs 'ferry.navigate' do Eng and PM prefer?
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype reviewed by PM/Eng and UX writing
Keyboard shortcut opens ferry and focus lands on first destination
Compact cost lane renders with live metrics from mocked endpoint and respects responsive breakpoints
Rollout actions open focused modal with confirm flows and audit-link placeholder
implementation_notes:
- Frontend: lightweight overlay component built with existing flyout primitives; aim to reuse console design tokens and motion timing.
- Backend: will consume existing /workspaces/summary endpoint; if missing fields, Eng to add aggregated metrics fields.
- Telemetry: events: ferry.open, ferry.select, lane.pin, lane.collapse, rollout.open, rollout.confirm.
- QA: automated E2E for keyboard nav, plus manual a11y pass.
risks:
- If backend metrics are delayed, compact lane may show stale data leading to confusion.
- Screen-reader ferry focus management requires careful QA to avoid focus traps.
- Pinning behavior may conflict with existing workspace favorites; we need PM alignment.
rollout_plan: 1) Dark-launch ferry behind feature flag for 10% of orgs. 2) Collect qualitative feedback over 2 weeks and telemetry for clicks/time-to-switch. 3) Iterate microcopy and affordances. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% with docs and in-console tips.
